column5: Counterpart says “Never end turn with uncommitted work in tree” and checks git status.
Siduri’s acceptance/W2/a6-rename.md and contract paths make renaming a contract file’s references a local guard.
Siduri’s AGENTS.md binds Codex workers to the task file rather than skill or CLAUDE.md; no counterpart sets that worker reading boundary.
Siduri’s AGENTS.md and its 32768-byte worker-file cap make silent truncation a local Codex contract, not another repo’s rule.
Siduri’s eight-lane model requires a named integration lane and task; the comparison rules do not define integration as lane residue.
Counterpart says a parallel package split gets one “Done-when that is end-to-end act by a person,” matching Siduri’s wave rule.
Siduri’s eight-lane split and green make check composition determine the unit of work; no counterpart makes gate-green the unit.
Siduri’s tools/acceptance.py consumes pinned acceptance fields, making parser-shaped task output a local artifact contract.
Siduri’s eight-lane Templ-versus-Go ownership changes the Done-when count; no counterpart varies that count by lane ownership.
Counterpart says “ran is command line, not description of one,” the same requirement that a command field be rerunnable rather than prose.
Siduri’s eight-lane one-commit boundary and lead-assigned subject are local lane workflow; the near miss says one step, one commit.
Siduri’s task contract and fresh-init incident concern stating this worktree’s branch; no counterpart governs branch facts in a task.
Counterpart says “Commit message two -m flags” with subject under 72 characters and body max six lines.
Counterpart says “Never ship command not run here, or whose flag was not read from binary here.”
Counterpart says “Definition of done is a list cited by range from the plan” and every line is met or deferred by name.
Counterpart says “Shared counter claimed in integration branch before work start” and unmerged allocation is not a claim.
The hitl installer/server swap and running-image digest incident is only reproducible in Siduri’s shared-host acceptance setup.
Parent .git/config identity before worktrees is Siduri’s worktree topology; no counterpart has this parent-config failure mode.
Counterpart says “Register is caveman lite: full sentence, article, technical term, code, command, error string, filename all survive.”
Counterpart says “Scan before send. Cut opener, filler, hedge, closer, tool narration.”
Counterpart says every reference carries its content in the same sentence every turn, not once per conversation.
Siduri’s AGENTS.md and make check enforce the 32768-byte worker contract; no counterpart sets this file-size cap.
Siduri’s internal/site rendering defects across chrome, meta, and width are this site’s cross-part failure class.
Siduri’s internal/site/build.go and ArticlePage workaround check is renderer-specific; no counterpart requires deleting that workaround.
Siduri’s make check guards must remain committed in this tree; the near matches cover reports or patches, not retained proof checks.
Siduri’s static build determinism is proved with a recursive dist-tree checksum; no counterpart specifies that site artifact measurement.
Siduri’s internal/site package-global registration can survive one build and requires a double-run test; that failure is local to this renderer.
Siduri’s tools/ guard fixtures must verify planted input landed and actual output, including frontmatter and secret scans; no counterpart states this checker self-test.
Counterpart says “Guard pinned to value it guard go red on correct work” and derives the target instead of naming it.
Siduri’s tools/secretscan.py exemption and acceptance/ record roles make exemption follow directory role; no counterpart has this path policy.
Counterpart says “Fact leaving this session carry where it was read from,” with file references, query commands, and units.
Counterpart says “Probe this turn beat every document” and treats an undated machine claim as a hypothesis.
Counterpart says “Never restate machine fact or code fact from memory” and opens the owning file that turn.
Siduri’s acceptance/census TSV contract requires grouped verdict equality and exact row partition; no counterpart has these two table invariants.
Counterpart says “Session is three phase, in order: carry-in close, one step, reflection,” matching work and record deposit.
Counterpart says “Never assert where session sit in own context” because harness summarisation makes the position unmeasurable.
Siduri’s two requirement documents can contradict an operator instruction, so this named contradiction rule belongs to its contract.
Counterpart says “Observation whose evidence a later action erase carry its date and that action in the sentence.”
Siduri’s two requirement documents and census scope need checked-versus-unchecked agreement boundaries; no counterpart requires this agreement record.
Counterpart says “A peer's claim is a claim until re-derived,” including the load-bearing half and which half was checked.
